x-e-e4-01.title: Mom's note and Jisu's playtime
x-e-e4-01.topic: A short note and a schedule
x-e-e4-01.goal: Compare the several plans on Mom's note with the time a friend suggested, find where they do not fit, and say no in English while suggesting a different time.
x-e-e4-01.material:
A note Mom left on the table (written as text only, with no picture):

Mina,
Today's plan:
3:30 p.m. Come home.
4:00 p.m. Piano class (30 minutes).
5:00 p.m. Take out the trash.
6:30 p.m. Dinner with Mom and Dad.

Then her friend Jisu sent a text. "Let's play at the park from 4:15 to 5:15 today!"
x-e-e4-01.thinking.0: Compare the times on the note with the suggested time range, one by one
x-e-e4-01.thinking.1: Judge whether a time 'range' and a single time overlap
x-e-e4-01.thinking.2: Tell it in English, giving your evidence
x-e-e4-01.prereq.0: The meaning of p.m. and reading times (like 3:30 and 4:00)
x-e-e4-01.prereq.1: Easy words such as piano class and trash
x-e-e4-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the lines of the note that overlap in time with Jisu's suggestion (4:15-5:15).
x-e-e4-01.s.s1.hint.0: Put each line next to the park time '4:15-5:15' one by one, and see whether it ends before or starts after.
x-e-e4-01.s.s1.hint.1: For things that take time, like a class, work out the time they end.
x-e-e4-01.s.s1.r.a: Compare whether the time you come home is before or after 4:15.
x-e-e4-01.s.s1.r.b: Work out what time the class starts and what time it ends, and put it next to the park time.
x-e-e4-01.s.s1.r.c: I thought of it as checking whether a single time falls inside the park time range.
x-e-e4-01.s.s1.r.d: Compare whether the dinner time is after the park time ends.
x-e-e4-01.s.s1.explain: Piano class is 4:00-4:30, so 4:15-4:30 overlaps, and taking out the trash at 5:00 falls within 4:15-5:15. Coming home at 3:30 and dinner at 6:30 are outside the park time.
x-e-e4-01.s.s2.prompt: Reply to Jisu in two or three English sentences. Find the reasons on the note why you cannot go, write them, and suggest one other time that works.
x-e-e4-01.s.s2.hint.0: First, say no in one sentence with 'Sorry, I can't ...'.
x-e-e4-01.s.s2.hint.1: Write the two overlapping plans from the note with their times, and at the end make your suggestion with 'Can we play at ...?'.
x-e-e4-01.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you give both reasons, piano and taking out the trash?
x-e-e4-01.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you suggest a different time, and does that time not overlap with the plans on the note?
x-e-e4-01.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Is there a refusing phrase like 'I can't'?
x-e-e4-01.s.s2.modelNote.1: A good reply that suggested the time as a range.

x-e-e4-02.title: Decide dog walk and homework times
x-e-e4-02.topic: A short note and a schedule
x-e-e4-02.goal: Make several different combinations of a walk time and a homework time that meet all the conditions on Dad's note.
x-e-e4-02.material:
A note Dad left (written as text only, with no picture):

Mina,
You come home at 4:00 p.m. I come home at 6:30 p.m.
- Walk the dog for 30 minutes. Not before 5:00 p.m. It is too hot.
- Do your homework for 60 minutes.
- Finish both before I come home.
- Do not do both at the same time.

Below, write each time as 'how many minutes after 4:00 p.m.'. For example, if you start at 4:30, write 30, and if you start at 5:15, write 75.
x-e-e4-02.thinking.0: Make an answer that meets several conditions at the same time yourself
x-e-e4-02.thinking.1: Add the time it takes to the start time to check the end time
x-e-e4-02.thinking.2: Check whether they overlap each other
x-e-e4-02.prereq.0: Reading times and adding in minutes
x-e-e4-02.prereq.1: Easy words such as walk the dog and homework
x-e-e4-02.s.s1.prompt: If Mina starts homework at 5:00 and the walk at 5:30, which condition on the note does she break?
x-e-e4-02.s.s1.hint.0: Add the time it takes (in minutes) to each task's start time to find the time it ends.
x-e-e4-02.s.s1.hint.1: Draw the time ranges of the two tasks side by side on one line.
x-e-e4-02.s.s1.r.a: Compare whether the walk start time 5:30 is before or after 5:00.
x-e-e4-02.s.s1.r.b: Put homework 5:00-6:00 and the walk 5:30-6:00 side by side on a timeline.
x-e-e4-02.s.s1.r.c: Find the end times of the two tasks by adding the time each takes to its start time.
x-e-e4-02.s.s1.r.d: This is a condition about how long the task takes, not about the start time.
x-e-e4-02.s.s1.explain: Homework is 5:00-6:00 and the walk is 5:30-6:00, so the two tasks overlap from 5:30 to 6:00. The walk starts after 5:00 and both finish before 6:30, so the other conditions are kept.
x-e-e4-02.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different plans that keep all the conditions on the note. w is the walk start and k is the homework start (how many minutes after 4:00 p.m.).
x-e-e4-02.s.s2.hint.0: First decide the range w can be for the walk start, then choose the homework start k so that it avoids that walk time.
x-e-e4-02.s.s2.hint.1: Find the end time from each task's start plus the time it takes, and check whether the two tasks overlap.
x-e-e4-02.s.s2.ok.c1: The time is in the right form.
x-e-e4-02.s.s2.fail.c1: Write w and k as whole numbers (minutes) that are 0 or more.
x-e-e4-02.s.s2.fail.c3: The walk or the homework ends after 6:30.
x-e-e4-02.s.s2.ok.c4: The two tasks do not overlap.
x-e-e4-02.s.s2.fail.c4: The walk and the homework times overlap.
x-e-e4-02.s.s2.explain: The walk must start between 60 and 120 minutes (5:00-6:00), and the homework must start within 90 minutes (by 5:30). Among those, the combinations that do not overlap are the answers. Examples: (walk 60, homework 0), (walk 90, homework 0), (walk 60, homework 90).

x-e-e4-03.title: Ken's text: read it line by line and guess his feelings
x-e-e4-03.goal: Each time you read a line of the text, guess again what your friend wants, and change your earlier guess with the new clues.
x-e-e4-03.material: Your friend Ken sends a text. It will be shown one piece at a time. For each piece, guess what Ken wants from you.
x-e-e4-03.thinking.0: Change your guess each time the clues grow
x-e-e4-03.thinking.1: Know that one sentence alone is not enough to tell
x-e-e4-03.thinking.2: Write an English reply using the reason (clues) as evidence
x-e-e4-03.prereq.0: Easy words such as cold and camp
x-e-e4-03.prereq.1: The meanings of 'play a game' and 'at home'
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.prompt: Read Ken's text one piece at a time, and each time guess what Ken wants.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.hint.0: Find one new word or number in this piece.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.hint.1: Check your earlier guess against the new clues, one by one, to see whether it still fits all of them.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: Choose all the reasonable guesses about what Ken wants from this one line alone.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.0.after: You cannot know exactly from one line alone. He could be just sharing news, or he could be asking to play together.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.0.o.a: He wants to tell me the news that he has a new game.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Only telling the news is also a possible reading.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.0.o.b: He wants to sell me a game.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.0.o.c: It seems he is about to ask me to play the game with him.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: It could be that he wants to do it together. For now, the clue is a weak guess.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.1.ask: Look at the new clue too, and guess again what Ken wants.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.1.after: Putting together 'a game for two players' and 'his brother goes to camp', the most natural reading is that he is looking for someone to play with.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.1.o.a: It seems he is thinking of me as the second person to play the game with.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Both the clue 'a game for two players' and the clue 'he has no brother' connect to this guess.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.1.o.b: He wants to play the game alone.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: It does not fit the clue 'two players'.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.1.o.c: He still only wants to tell me the news.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: It was possible from the first line, but now that the clue that he has nobody to play with has been added, it no longer explains all the clues.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.2.ask: Look at the last clue too, and guess again what Ken wants.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.2.after: If you first guessed 'let's play together', now you must change it from 'today' to 'later'. One new clue (a cold, Mom's words) changed the plan.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.2.o.a: He is asking me to come to his house today and play together.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: It does not fit the clue that his mom said friends cannot come to the house today.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.2.o.b: He does not want to play with me anymore.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: He gave the reason for saying no (a cold, Mom's words), and there is no clue that he does not want to play.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.2.o.c: He wants to play together when he gets better.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: The cold is the reason, so this is the reading that it will be possible when the cold is gone.
x-e-e4-03.s.s1.reflect: Of your three guesses, where did it change the most? Name one sentence that was the reason.
x-e-e4-03.s.s2.prompt: Reply to Ken in one or two English sentences. It should show that you understood what Ken wants.
x-e-e4-03.s.s2.hint.0: First write one sentence about Ken's health.
x-e-e4-03.s.s2.hint.1: In the second sentence, suggest when to play the game together.
x-e-e4-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you acknowledge Ken's cold or suggest doing it later?
x-e-e4-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you follow up on Ken's game?
x-e-e4-03.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Is there anything that does not fit the earlier clues, like saying you will go to his house today?
x-e-e4-03.s.s2.modelNote.1: A reply that suggested a specific time.

x-e-e4-04.title: What is Sora's email asking for?
x-e-e4-04.goal: Judge the writer's intention in a short email, giving your evidence, and answer in English to fit that intention.
x-e-e4-04.material:
An email Sora sent to her teacher (written as text only, with no picture):

Dear Ms. Park,
I am sorry. I forgot my homework at home. My mom can bring it to school at 11 a.m. today. Is that OK?
Sora

Three friends said what Sora wants.
x-e-e4-04.thinking.0: Choose the claim with better evidence among different claims
x-e-e4-04.thinking.1: Infer the intention from the words of the email
x-e-e4-04.prereq.0: Easy words such as homework and bring
x-e-e4-04.prereq.1: That 'Is that OK?' is a way of asking for permission
x-e-e4-04.s.s1.prompt: Whose reading fits the sentences of the email best?
x-e-e4-04.s.s1.hint.0: Check the three readings against the sentences of the email, one by one, and find the words that clash.
x-e-e4-04.s.s1.hint.1: Write down what each of 'bring', 'today', and 'Is that OK?' tells you.
x-e-e4-04.s.s1.o.a: Min: "Sora wants to not hand in her homework."
x-e-e4-04.s.s1.r.a: Look for whether the email says she will bring the homework.
x-e-e4-04.s.s1.o.b: Jun: "Sora is asking for more time until tomorrow."
x-e-e4-04.s.s1.r.b: Check which word is in the email, today or tomorrow.
x-e-e4-04.s.s1.o.c: Hana: "Sora is asking whether she may hand in her homework this morning."
x-e-e4-04.s.s1.r.c: Look at what '11 a.m. today' and 'Is that OK?' point to together.
x-e-e4-04.s.s1.explain: 'My mom can bring it ... at 11 a.m. today' says she will bring the homework at 11 this morning, and 'Is that OK?' asks whether that is all right. There are no words about not handing it in, and none about asking for it until tomorrow.
x-e-e4-04.s.s2.prompt: Be Ms. Park and reply to Sora in one or two English sentences. Answer Sora's question.
x-e-e4-04.s.s2.hint.0: First, answer Sora's question with 'Yes' or 'No'.
x-e-e4-04.s.s2.hint.1: In the second sentence, write when and to whom she should give the homework.
x-e-e4-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you answer Sora's question (Is that OK?)?
x-e-e4-04.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you write the time or way of bringing the homework so that it fits the email?
x-e-e4-04.s.s2.selfAssess.2: If your answer does not give permission, did you write the reason?
x-e-e4-04.s.s2.modelNote.1: A reply that gives permission and even adds a reminder for next time.

x-e-e4-05.title: Can I go on Movie Day?
x-e-e4-05.goal: Separate the information needed to decide from the information that is not, and judge from the information you get whether you can go.
x-e-e4-05.material:
A notice on the school board (written as text only, with no picture):

Movie Day
Friday, after school
Come and watch a movie in the gym.
Bring a snack.

Mina's situation: On Friday she has to be home by 6:00 p.m., and it takes 20 minutes to walk from school to home. The money she can spend is 1,000원.
x-e-e4-05.thinking.0: Compare with my own conditions and choose the information that is really needed
x-e-e4-05.thinking.1: Check whether the information you got meets all the conditions
x-e-e4-05.thinking.2: Tell interesting information from needed information
x-e-e4-05.prereq.1: Easy words such as ticket, movie, and snack
x-e-e4-05.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the information Mina must ask the teacher about to decide whether she can go.
x-e-e4-05.s.s1.hint.0: First write down Mina's two conditions, and then find what information is missing from the notice.
x-e-e4-05.s.s1.hint.1: For each question, think about whether its answer could change 'go' or 'not go'.
x-e-e4-05.s.s1.r.a: Information you are curious about and information you need to decide are different. Think about whether you could check the time and money even without this information.
x-e-e4-05.s.s1.r.b: This is information that connects to the time condition among Mina's conditions.
x-e-e4-05.s.s1.r.c: This is information that connects to the money condition among Mina's conditions.
x-e-e4-05.s.s1.r.d: The notice already has 'Bring a snack.' Think about whether this answer changes whether she goes or not.
x-e-e4-05.s.s1.explain: Mina has two conditions, 'get home by 6' and '1,000원', so she can only decide whether to go when she knows the time the movie ends and the price of the ticket. The name of the movie and the snack are things to be curious about, but they do not change the decision.
x-e-e4-05.s.s2.prompt: The teacher answered. "The movie ends at 5:30 p.m. A ticket is 1,500 won." What should Mina do?
x-e-e4-05.s.s2.hint.0: Check the two conditions separately, one at a time.
x-e-e4-05.s.s2.hint.1: Check the time condition by adding the walking time to the end time.
x-e-e4-05.s.s2.o.a: Money and time are both fine, so she can go.
x-e-e4-05.s.s2.r.a: Check whether you compared the money condition with the ticket price you were given.
x-e-e4-05.s.s2.o.b: When the movie ends she will be late and cannot get home by 6.
x-e-e4-05.s.s2.r.b: Add the 20 minutes of walking to 5:30 and compare it with 6:00.
x-e-e4-05.s.s2.o.c: The time is fine, but she does not have enough money.
x-e-e4-05.s.s2.r.c: This is thinking that checked the two conditions separately.
x-e-e4-05.s.s2.explain: It ends at 5:30, and with a 20-minute walk she arrives at 5:50, which is before 6:00. But the ticket is 1,500원, so she cannot buy it with 1,000원. You need to check both conditions.

x-e-e4-06.title: What should I ask Ben?
x-e-e4-06.goal: Find the information missing from a plan, and make two English questions yourself to get that information.
x-e-e4-06.material:
Ben sent Mina a text: "Let's do our science homework together on Saturday. Come to my house!"

Mina's situation: Ben moved to a new house, and Mina does not know where the new house is. Mina has a swimming class on Saturday from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m.
x-e-e4-06.thinking.0: Separate the missing information from the information you already know
x-e-e4-06.thinking.1: Make questions that get the missing information
x-e-e4-06.thinking.2: Write questions that reflect my own conditions
x-e-e4-06.prereq.0: Making what time, where, and how questions
x-e-e4-06.prereq.1: Reading the short sentences of the text
x-e-e4-06.s.s1.prompt: To make a plan, choose all the information Mina must ask Ben about.
x-e-e4-06.s.s1.hint.0: Write down separately the information that is in Ben's text and the information that is not.
x-e-e4-06.s.s1.hint.1: From Mina's two situations, find what she still does not know.
x-e-e4-06.s.s1.r.a: This is information that connects to Mina's Saturday schedule.
x-e-e4-06.s.s1.o.b: What Ben ate in the morning
x-e-e4-06.s.s1.r.b: Even if you are curious, think about whether it is information you need to make the plan.
x-e-e4-06.s.s1.o.c: How to get to Ben's new house, or the address
x-e-e4-06.s.s1.r.c: This is information that connects to something Mina still does not know in her situation.
x-e-e4-06.s.s1.r.d: The subject is already in Ben's text. Check whether you need to find it out again.
x-e-e4-06.s.s1.explain: There is no time, so she cannot tell whether it overlaps with the swimming class, and she does not know where the new house is, so she cannot go. The homework subject (science) is in the text, and breakfast has nothing to do with the plan.
x-e-e4-06.s.s2.prompt: Write two English questions to send to Ben. One question must be about the time and the other about the place.
x-e-e4-06.s.s2.hint.0: First choose the question words. A time question can start with What time, and a place question can start with Where or How.
x-e-e4-06.s.s2.hint.1: Put a question mark (?) at the end of each question, and think about whether you can ask about the time more specifically because of the swimming class.
x-e-e4-06.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Is one question about the time and one about the place?
x-e-e4-06.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Because of my swimming class (10-11), could I make the time question more specific?
x-e-e4-06.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you put a question mark at the end of the sentences?
x-e-e4-06.s.s2.modelNote.1: A specific question that reflects the swimming class.

x-e-e4-07.title: Two libraries, one sentence

x-e-e4-07.thinking.0: Find the sentence that caused the misunderstanding
x-e-e4-07.thinking.1: Work out the missing information (which library)
x-e-e4-07.thinking.2: Check whether the rewritten sentence adds the information
x-e-e4-07.prereq.0: Easy words such as library, school, and park
x-e-e4-07.s.s1.prompt: Which line has the words that made the two friends fail to meet each other?
x-e-e4-07.s.s1.hint.0: Check in lines 3 and 4 where Jisu and Ben each are.
x-e-e4-07.s.s1.hint.1: Find which line has the word that made the two of them picture different places.
x-e-e4-07.s.s1.explain: 'The library' in line 1 does not tell you whether it is the City Library or the school library. The grammar is right, but the place is missing, so the two of them went to different libraries.
x-e-e4-07.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite line 1 in English so that Ben can come to where Jisu is. Keep the day and the time as they are.
x-e-e4-07.s.s2.hint.0: Think about what place Ben pictures when he reads 'the library'.
x-e-e4-07.s.s2.hint.1: Add one more phrase before or after 'library' that tells the place (a name, a nearby place, etc.).
x-e-e4-07.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Can you tell which library it is right away?
x-e-e4-07.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you keep the day and the time of the original sentence as they are?
x-e-e4-07.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Does Ben not need to ask again after he reads it?
x-e-e4-07.s.s2.modelNote.1: An answer that tells the place in two ways and even decides where to meet.

x-e-e4-08.title: Who is 'she'?

x-e-e4-08.material:
Hana sent Jisu a text: "Mina told Sora that she has the glue."

x-e-e4-08.thinking.0: Find all the people a pronoun could refer to
x-e-e4-08.thinking.2: Fix it into a sentence without misunderstanding
x-e-e4-08.prereq.0: Basic words such as she, he, and told
x-e-e4-08.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the people 'she' could refer to in Hana's sentence.
x-e-e4-08.s.s1.hint.0: Count how many names appear in the sentence.
x-e-e4-08.s.s1.hint.1: Find all the girls' names that come before she.
x-e-e4-08.s.s1.r.a: Hana is the person who wrote the sentence. Check whether her name appears inside the sentence.
x-e-e4-08.s.s1.r.b: This is the person who comes before 'told' in the sentence.
x-e-e4-08.s.s1.r.c: The person who comes after 'told' could also be 'she'.
x-e-e4-08.s.s1.r.d: This is the person who got the text. Check whether the name appears inside the sentence.

x-e-e4-08.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Is it clear that there is only one person to bring the glue?
x-e-e4-08.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Is there nothing that could confuse people again, like a pronoun such as 'she' or 'her'?
x-e-e4-08.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Does it have the same meaning as what Mina originally said (Sora brings it)?
x-e-e4-08.s.s2.modelNote.1: A natural answer that used indirect speech with 'to bring'.

x-e-e4-09.title: The same situation, two different people
x-e-e4-09.topic: Writing differently to a friend and a teacher
x-e-e4-09.goal: Write the same situation differently, as a text to a friend and as an email to a teacher.
x-e-e4-09.material: There is English speaking practice at school on Saturday morning. But you cannot go because you are going on a trip with your family that day. Write in English a text to tell your friend Jisu and an email to your teacher Ms. Kim.
x-e-e4-09.thinking.0: Change the greeting and tone depending on who receives it
x-e-e4-09.thinking.2: Tell a polite request from a casual tone
x-e-e4-09.prereq.0: Easy words such as can't, sorry, and trip

x-e-e4-10.title: Sending a text written to a friend to a teacher
x-e-e4-10.topic: Writing differently to a friend and a teacher
x-e-e4-10.goal: Find the parts of a text to a friend that do not suit a teacher, and rewrite the same situation to suit a teacher.
x-e-e4-10.material:
A text sent to the friend Jisu (written as text only, with no picture):

"Hey! I'm sick lol. Can't come 2 school 2morrow. Gimme the homework pls!"

(By the way, 2morrow is read 'tu-morrow', a short way of writing tomorrow.) You want to send the same content to your teacher by email.
x-e-e4-10.thinking.0: Find the expressions that do not suit who receives it
x-e-e4-10.thinking.1: Keep the situation (the reason) and change only the tone
x-e-e4-10.prereq.0: The meanings of sick, homework, and tomorrow
x-e-e4-10.prereq.1: How to read text message abbreviations
x-e-e4-10.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the parts that must be fixed when sending this text to a teacher.
x-e-e4-10.s.s1.hint.0: Read it out loud as if you were talking to a teacher.
x-e-e4-10.s.s1.hint.1: Look separately, one at a time, at the abbreviations, the slang, and the way of asking.
x-e-e4-10.s.s1.r.a: The reason for being sick is a situation you should tell the teacher too. Think about whether it should be changed or kept.
x-e-e4-10.s.s1.r.b: Compare the fact that the receiver is a teacher with the feeling of this expression.
x-e-e4-10.s.s1.r.c: Think about whether using numbers instead of words suits writing sent to a teacher.
x-e-e4-10.s.s1.r.d: Look at whether the way of asking suits a teacher.
x-e-e4-10.s.s1.explain: 'lol', '2 school 2morrow' shortened with numbers, and 'Gimme ... pls!' are the way friends talk to each other, so they must be fixed for a teacher. The reason for being sick ('I'm sick') is a situation to keep.
x-e-e4-10.s.s2.prompt: Rewrite the same content in English as an email to Ms. Kim. Start with a greeting, and include that you are sick, that you cannot come tomorrow, and a request to be told the homework.
x-e-e4-10.s.s2.hint.0: Keep as it is the part (the situation) that you did not choose in step 1.
x-e-e4-10.s.s2.hint.1: Change 'Gimme the homework' into a sentence that asks, like 'Could you please ...?'.
x-e-e4-10.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you start with a greeting that suits a teacher?
x-e-e4-10.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you remove all the friend abbreviations and slang?
x-e-e4-10.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Are both the situation (being sick) and the request (the homework) still there?
x-e-e4-10.s.s2.modelNote.1: An answer that even offered to get it from a friend.
